title: Knitted ear warmer headband
subtitle: A wide ribbed ear warmer worked flat and seamed, one adult size.
excerpt: A wide 2 x 2 rib ear warmer worked flat on straight or circular needles in aran yarn, then seamed into a band. Fits an adult head of 54 to 58 cm. Quick and warm for a first-time knitter.
sourceNotes: Knitted headband ear warmers are a modern pattern type with no significant public-domain precedent.

content.text: This knitted ear warmer headband is worked flat in
2 x 2 rib
and seamed at the back into a band, fitting adult heads of 54 to 58 cm.

Flat construction is chosen over working in the round because the cast-on edge of a flat piece has no twist risk and the short row count means the knitter can check length easily. The 2 x 2 rib stretches to fit heads from 54 cm to 58 cm from a single 56 cm length. About 50 g (90 m) of aran yarn. Covers the ears and forehead while leaving the top of the head free.
What you need

items.name: 5 mm needles (straight or circular), 35 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

18 sts x 24 rows = 10 x 10 cm in 2 x 2 rib (relaxed, not stretched) on 5 mm needles. An ear warmer is forgiving of gauge variation because 2 x 2 rib stretches readily. At 19 sts per 10 cm the finished band is 53 cm and still stretches to fit a 54 cm head; at 17 sts per 10 cm it is 59 cm, which will sit loose. Measure relaxed.
Stitches used
k -- knit
p -- purl
Pattern
This pattern is a single size.
Cast on

Cast on 18 sts using long-tail cast-on. The count must be a multiple of 4 plus 2 for the edges (18 = 4 x 4 + 2). Tail formula: tail_cm = (needle mm x stitch count) / 10 + 15. For 18 sts on a 5 mm needle: (5 x 18) / 10 + 15 = 24 cm; round up to 30 cm.
Body

Row 1 (right side): k2, *p2, k2; repeat from * to end. Row 2 (wrong side): p2, *k2, p2; repeat from * to end. Repeat rows 1 and 2 until piece measures 56 cm from cast-on edge. After completing the body, you should have 18 stitches on the needle.
Cast off
Cast off in pattern (k the k stitches, p the p stitches as you cast off) to keep the cast-off edge as elastic as the body. Do not cast off tightly.
Seam

Fold the band into a ring and align the cast-on edge with the cast-off edge. Seam using mattress stitch from the right side, working through the edge stitches alternately. Join and weave in both ends.
Common faults
Cast-off edge tighter than cast-on edge: the cast-off was worked too firmly. Always cast off in pattern on a needle one size larger than the body needle to match the stretch of the rib.
Seam shows on the outside: mattress stitch was drawn too tight. Work each stitch snugly but not pulled; the seam should disappear into the rib columns.

Band sits on top of the ears rather than covering them: the 10 cm width is at the limit of what looks like an ear warmer. If the knitter has a longer ear, add 4 more sts to the cast-on (22 sts) for a wider band.
Finishing
Weave in all ends. Wet-block lightly to even the rib columns; the band will spring back to its relaxed circumference when dry.
Care
Hand wash cool, squeeze without wringing, reshape and dry flat.
What to try next
The knitted headband uses a narrower, less stretchy stitch for a more structured look. Try the lace headband to add decorative openwork to the same band shape.
